acceptanceCriteria: A spec under docs/specs/ records intent, numbered requirements, identity rules, non-goals and rollback; intent stays proposed until the owner accepts it.
The same go test -json stream recorded twice yields byte-identical records and no duplicate entries.
Records name package, test and subtest path, tree, toolchain and platform; a renamed test is a new identity, never a silent merge.
Nothing feeds ranking or authority; NOT_RUN and NOT_OBSERVED stay explicit.
body: Idea source: Arize Phoenix (github.com/arize-ai/phoenix), reviewed 2026-10-05. Phoenix is Elastic License 2.0 with a patent notice, so this is a clean-room idea only: no Phoenix code, text or tests may be copied into AGPL Corvint. Idea: keep the existing Go test suite as the source of truth and derive evaluation records from go test -json output instead of hand-authored eval rows (product invariant 6). Tests are not uniform (different packages, subtests, repeat counts) and no aggregate gate is computed; instead hold strict: (a) stable identity per package, test and subtest path, bound to the immutable tree; (b) non-duplicating, idempotent writes on rerun; (c) provenance naming the command, toolchain, platform and tree. Payoff: flaky tests (V1-0768, V1-0771, V1-0815, V1-0724, V1-0779, V1-0796) gain a durable cross-run identity and history, so flake rates are measured, not remembered. Related: V1-0245 (gate-ledger per-package pass recording). Any ledger must respect invariant 4 (read commands do not mutate) and must not feed ranking.
title: Derive evaluation evidence from go test -json with stable test identity ("relax uniformity, never identity")
